raw_response:
I will still farm close to what I know, not make big changes all at once. I have done this many years, so I start from last year’s way and then adjust a little by price, weather, and what I saw around me. On 9 mu, I cannot gamble. Cotton takes more watching and more pesticide, but if I manage it well, it still brings cash, so I will keep some land in cotton. Maize is steadier and easier for labor, especially when some family members work outside, so I will put the larger share into maize. With well irrigation in hand, I do not want seedlings to suffer dry weather early. For fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than let the crop go hungry. For cotton, I will use a little more potash because bolls need strength, and I will split nitrogen so it does not grow too wild at the start. For maize, I will feed it enough at the base and then topdress once when it grows fast. I watch what nearby farmers do, and around here improved cotton seed and hybrid maize usually give more stable yield, so I will use those, not old seed saved at home.
